newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH rebounds as market ponders strategy.
newsitem.headline: LVMH rebounds as market ponders strategy.

text.p: Shares in luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton rebounded on Friday, recovering the ground lost since the company began buying up Grand Metropolitan stock this week.
LVMH shares finished up 4.79 percent at 1,531 francs.

Some analysts say they sympathise with LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault's criticisms of the planned merger between Guinness and Grand Met and see value in his proposal to group the three companies' drinks businesses and spin off the brewing, canned vegetable and fast-food operations.
But some brokers are wary and say LVMH risks taking on a lot of debt in its effort to thwart the deal, which also faces possible complications on antitrust grounds.
It has paid about 790 million stg to raise its stake in Grand Met to 6.3 percent and is expected to increase its holding.
"They paid 18 billion francs to buy DFS and this could end up costing them 15 billion," one broker estimated.
Standard & Poor's put LVMH's A-1-plus commercial paper rating on credit watch with negative implications.
Analysts say LVMH appears to be trying to force Guinness and Grand Met -- it is now the biggest shareholder in both -- to seriously consider its alternative proposal.

It could block the merger outright if it owned more than 24 percent of Grand Met, or it could call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting and put its proposal to the other shareholders with just 10 percent, analysts say.
LVMH declined to comment. But it said earlier this week it was not launching a buyout bid for Grand Met.
U.S. regulators asked the British companies for more information about the merger on Friday and European Union authorities opened a full probe into the antitrust implications.

The merger would bring under one roof Johnnie Walker and Bell's whisky, Gordon's Gin, Smirnoff vodka, Guinness's traditional stout and Dewar's. LVMH's drinks labels include Pommery and Moet & Chandon champagnes and Hennessy cognacs.
